argument: When a gauge-coupled field acquires a nonzero vacuum expectation value, would-be Goldstone modes combine with gauge fields to produce massive vector excitations while preserving the underlying gauge consistency. Residual scalar excitations include the Higgs boson.
boundary: The mechanism requires a suitable field content, potential, and symmetry-breaking vacuum.
The observed Higgs sector does not by itself explain all particle masses or hierarchy questions.
Gauge symmetry is not literally destroyed; the physical description depends on gauge and phase.
claim: When a gauge-coupled field acquires a nonzero vacuum expectation value, would-be Goldstone modes combine with gauge fields to produce massive vector excitations while preserving the underlying gauge consistency. Residual scalar excitations include the Higgs boson.
interpretation: The Meta-Principle links symmetry, collective vacuum state, and effective mass; it should not be generalized to every form of symmetry breaking.

migration_provenance.source_basics: Several groups formulated the mechanism in 1964. The Higgs boson was observed at CERN in 2012, and Englert and Higgs received the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics.
